validation.notes: Lotes 1–4 curated for Teacher Israel Ventura. Original workplace English only (not ETS material). 16 sets / 67 questions. Lote 1: email, ad, article, chat+notice. Lote 2: memo, letter, form, email+notice. Lote 3: article, ad, invoice, chat+notice. Lote 4: email, memo, letter, email+notice+form (first triple).

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Subject: Update on order #48219 — delivery delay
passages.body:
Dear Mr. Delgado,

I am writing regarding your order of twelve ergonomic chairs for the Westside branch. The shipment was scheduled to leave our warehouse on Monday, but a supplier shortage has delayed production of the adjustable armrests.

We now expect the chairs to ship on Friday and to arrive at your location by next Wednesday. As a courtesy, we will include two free lumbar cushions and waive the express shipping fee on this order.

If next Wednesday is too late for your staff move-in, please reply by Thursday noon so we can transfer you to our rental inventory for two weeks at no charge.

We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience.

Sincerely,
Aisha Rahman
Fulfillment Coordinator, SeatWell Office

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this email?

options.text: To confirm that twelve chairs have already been delivered
To explain a shipping delay and offer remedies
To request payment for express shipping
To announce a permanent change in armrest design

questions.correctAnswer: To explain a shipping delay and offer remedies
questions.explanation: The email reports a delay caused by a supplier shortage and offers free cushions, waived fees, and optional rentals.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing only on the free cushions and missing that the core purpose is the delay update.

questions.question: According to the email, when are the chairs now expected to arrive?

options.text: This Monday
This Friday
Next Wednesday
Thursday noon

questions.correctAnswer: Next Wednesday
questions.explanation: The chairs will ship on Friday and arrive by next Wednesday. Thursday noon is the reply deadline for rentals.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the new ship date (Friday) with the arrival date (next Wednesday).

questions.question: In the email, the phrase “as a courtesy” is closest in meaning to

options.text: as a legal requirement
as a temporary loan
as a polite gesture
as a final warning

questions.correctAnswer: as a polite gesture
questions.explanation: “As a courtesy” introduces goodwill extras (free cushions, waived fee) offered to soften the inconvenience.
questions.commonMistake: Reading “courtesy” as something owed by contract rather than a goodwill offer.

questions.question: What must Mr. Delgado do if he wants temporary rental chairs?

options.text: Pay the express shipping fee in advance
Reply by Thursday noon
Visit the SeatWell warehouse on Monday
Cancel order #48219 immediately

questions.correctAnswer: Reply by Thursday noon
questions.explanation: The email says to reply by Thursday noon so the company can transfer him to rental inventory at no charge.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming he must cancel the original order; the email offers rentals as a bridge, not a cancellation.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Harbor Desk — Flexible desks for growing teams
passages.body:
Looking for a professional workspace without a long lease?

Harbor Desk offers hot desks, private offices, and meeting rooms in the Riverfront district. Members enjoy high-speed Wi-Fi, printing credits, complimentary coffee, and 24-hour key-card access.

Spring offer for new annual members (through April 30):
• First month free on any private office
• Two guest day passes each month
• 15% off weekday meeting-room bookings

Tour our third-floor loft this Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Reserve a spot at harbordesk.example/tour or call (555) 014-2280.

Current day-pass holders are welcome but do not qualify for the spring discount.

questions.question: What is this advertisement mainly promoting?

options.text: A spring membership deal at a coworking space
A coffee shop opening in the Riverfront district
A weekend technology conference
A long-term residential lease program

questions.correctAnswer: A spring membership deal at a coworking space
questions.explanation: The ad presents Harbor Desk workspace options and a spring offer for new annual members through April 30.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing on complimentary coffee and treating the ad as a café promotion.

questions.question: When can interested people tour the third-floor loft?

options.text: Any weekday after 2:00 p.m.
Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
Only on April 30
24 hours a day with a key card

questions.correctAnswer: Saturday from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
questions.explanation: The ad explicitly invites a Saturday tour from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Key-card access is a member benefit, not the tour time.
questions.commonMistake: Mixing member 24-hour access with the scheduled public tour hours.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the spring offer for new annual members?

options.text: First month free on a private office
Two guest day passes each month
15% off weekday meeting-room bookings
Unlimited free printing for guests

questions.correctAnswer: Unlimited free printing for guests
questions.explanation: A–C are listed in the spring offer. The ad mentions printing credits for members, not unlimited free guest printing.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming printing credits equal unlimited free printing for guests.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Northline Logistics pilots on-site wellness coaches
passages.body:
Northline Logistics has launched a six-month pilot that places certified wellness coaches at its two largest distribution hubs. Employees can book 20-minute sessions during lunch breaks to discuss sleep habits, stress, and simple stretches for warehouse work.

Participation is voluntary and free. Early figures show that about 40 percent of day-shift workers at the Lakeside hub have booked at least one session. Night-shift staff may join starting next month, when evening coach hours will be added.

HR director Elena Vargas said the company will survey participants in September before deciding whether to expand the program to smaller sites. Managers are asked not to require attendance or to track who skips sessions.

“We want people to feel supported, not monitored,” Vargas noted. Coaches will also run a monthly workshop open to all employees, including remote office staff who can attend by video.

questions.question: How long is the wellness-coach pilot scheduled to last?

options.text: 20 minutes
One month
Six months
Until September only

questions.correctAnswer: Six months
questions.explanation: The article opens by stating Northline has launched a six-month pilot. Twenty minutes is the session length, not the program length.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing session length (20 minutes) with the pilot duration.

questions.question: What can be inferred about night-shift workers at the start of the pilot?

options.text: They already make up 40 percent of bookings.
They cannot yet book coach sessions during their shift hours.
They must attend the monthly workshop in person.
They are required to complete a September survey.

questions.correctAnswer: They cannot yet book coach sessions during their shift hours.
questions.explanation: Night-shift staff may join starting next month when evening coach hours are added — implying they are not covered yet.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming the 40% Lakeside figure includes night-shift workers.

questions.question: In the article, the word “voluntary” most nearly means

options.text: required by managers
done by choice
paid by the employee
limited to remote staff

questions.correctAnswer: done by choice
questions.explanation: Participation is voluntary and free, and managers must not require attendance — so employees join by choice.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing “voluntary” with “unpaid” because of similar Spanish false friends.

questions.question: What is the article mainly about?

options.text: A temporary wellness-coach program at Northline hubs
A permanent company-wide sleep clinic
A new rule requiring stretch breaks every hour
A plan to close smaller distribution sites

questions.correctAnswer: A temporary wellness-coach program at Northline hubs
questions.explanation: The piece describes a six-month pilot at two hubs, with a September review before any expansion.
questions.commonMistake: Overgeneralizing to a permanent company-wide program before the survey decision.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Team chat — Project Orion kickoff
passages.body:
Mia Chen: Can someone grab Maple Room for Thursday 2–4 p.m.? We need a screen for the vendor demo.
Sam Ortiz: I just checked the portal — Maple is free then. Want me to book it under Orion?
Mia Chen: Yes please. Also invite Facilities so they bring the extra HDMI cable.
Sam Ortiz: Booked. Confirmation #MR-4418. I’ll ping Facilities now.
Priya Nair: Heads-up — I saw a building notice about AV testing on Thursday afternoon. Might affect Maple.
Sam Ortiz: Thanks. I’ll read the notice and move us if needed.

passages.label: B
passages.heading: Facilities notice — Thursday AV system testing
passages.body:
TO: All staff
FROM: Facilities Services
DATE: March 11
SUBJECT: Audiovisual testing — Thursday, March 14

Facilities will test upgraded projectors and wireless display adapters in Maple Room and Cedar Room on Thursday, March 14, from 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.

During this window, screen sharing may be interrupted without notice. Meetings that require a stable display should be relocated to Willow Room (available all afternoon) or rescheduled.

Bookings already confirmed for Maple or Cedar during the test will remain in the portal, but Facilities cannot guarantee AV performance. For help moving a reservation, email rooms@northline.example or use confirmation lookup in the booking portal.

Thank you for your flexibility.
Facilities Services

questions.question: What confirmation number did Sam receive for the Maple Room booking?

options.text: HDMI-20
Orion-314

questions.explanation: In the chat, Sam says the booking is confirmed as #MR-4418.
questions.commonMistake: Inventing a number from the project name or test times.

questions.question: According to the notice, how long will the audiovisual testing last?

options.text: From 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
From 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
All day on March 14
Only during lunch

questions.correctAnswer: From 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
questions.explanation: The notice states testing in Maple and Cedar on March 14 from 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
questions.commonMistake: Using the meeting time from the chat (2–4 p.m.) instead of the notice window.

questions.question: Why does Priya mention the building notice in the chat?

options.text: She wants to cancel the vendor demo permanently.
She is warning that Maple’s display may be unreliable Thursday afternoon.
She needs an HDMI cable for Willow Room.
She is confirming that Cedar Room is already booked for Orion.

questions.correctAnswer: She is warning that Maple’s display may be unreliable Thursday afternoon.
questions.explanation: Priya flags a notice about AV testing Thursday afternoon that might affect Maple — a caution about display reliability.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming she is canceling the meeting rather than raising a risk.

questions.question: Based on the chat and the notice, what is the best next step for the Orion meeting?

options.text: Keep Maple Room and ignore the notice because the booking is confirmed
Move the demo to Willow Room or another time to ensure a stable screen
Switch the meeting to Cedar Room at the same time
Ask Facilities to stop testing until after 4:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswer: Move the demo to Willow Room or another time to ensure a stable screen
questions.explanation: The chat needs a screen for a vendor demo during 2–4 p.m.; the notice warns Maple AV may fail 1:30–3:30 and recommends Willow or rescheduling. Cedar is also under test.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing Cedar — it is tested in the same window — or relying only on the portal confirmation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT stated in either passage?

options.text: Maple Room was booked for Thursday 2–4 p.m.
Willow Room is available all Thursday afternoon
Facilities will bring an extra HDMI cable automatically
AV testing may interrupt screen sharing

questions.correctAnswer: Facilities will bring an extra HDMI cable automatically
questions.explanation: Mia asks to invite Facilities for an HDMI cable, but neither text confirms automatic delivery. A, B, and D are explicit in the chat or notice.
questions.commonMistake: Treating Mia’s request as a confirmed Facilities action.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: MEMO — Cafeteria closure for floor renovation
passages.body:
TO: All Cedar Heights employees
FROM: Facilities Operations
DATE: September 8
SUBJECT: Cafeteria closure for floor renovation

The employee cafeteria on Level 2 will be closed from Monday, September 15 through Friday, September 26 for flooring replacement and new serving-line equipment.

Temporary options during the closure:
• Food trucks in the west parking lot, 11:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m. weekdays
• Microwave stations and seating in the Level 1 lobby lounge
• 10% discount at Bistro North across the street with your employee badge

Vending machines on Levels 3 and 5 remain available. Catered meetings already booked in the cafeteria for those two weeks will be moved to Conference Suite B; organizers will receive a calendar update by September 10.

Please contact facilities@cedarheights.example with dietary or accessibility needs for the temporary setup.

Facilities Operations

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this memo?

options.text: To announce a temporary cafeteria closure and alternatives
To permanently close the Level 1 lobby lounge
To advertise a new restaurant owned by Cedar Heights
To require all employees to eat only from vending machines

questions.correctAnswer: To announce a temporary cafeteria closure and alternatives
questions.explanation: The memo explains a two-week Level 2 cafeteria closure for renovation and lists temporary food options and meeting moves.
questions.commonMistake: Treating the Bistro North discount as the main point instead of the closure announcement.

questions.question: When will the cafeteria be closed?

options.text: September 8 only
September 10 through September 15
September 15 through September 26
Every weekend in September

questions.correctAnswer: September 15 through September 26
questions.explanation: The memo states closure from Monday, September 15 through Friday, September 26. September 8 is the memo date; September 10 is the calendar-update deadline.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the memo date or the September 10 update deadline with the closure window.

questions.question: In the memo, the word “temporary” most nearly means

options.text: permanent
for a limited time
expensive
outdoor only

questions.correctAnswer: for a limited time
questions.explanation: “Temporary options during the closure” refers to arrangements that last only while the cafeteria is closed (Sept 15–26).
questions.commonMistake: Assuming temporary options are only the outdoor food trucks.

questions.question: What will happen to catered meetings that were booked in the cafeteria during the closure?

options.text: They will be canceled without notice
They will be moved to Conference Suite B
They will be held in the west parking lot
They must be rescheduled after September 26 by the organizers

questions.correctAnswer: They will be moved to Conference Suite B
questions.explanation: The memo says booked catered meetings will be moved to Conference Suite B, with calendar updates by September 10.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming organizers must reschedule themselves; Facilities is relocating the bookings.

sets.title: Quality apology for misaligned bottle labels

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Letter from ClearLabel Packaging Quality Manager
passages.body:
Dear Ms. Okonkwo,

Thank you for your letter of August 28 describing the misaligned labels on the last shipment of Apex bottles (PO-7731).

We inspected the returned samples and confirmed that a printer calibration error on Line B caused the defect. Line B has been recalibrated, and we have added a double-check step before packaging.

Replacement bottles for the full order of 2,400 units will ship tomorrow via overnight freight at no charge. You should receive them by Thursday. We will also credit your account $180 for the return shipping you arranged.

If you prefer a partial restock instead, please notify me by Tuesday at noon. We value your partnership with ClearLabel Packaging and apologize for the disruption to your production schedule.

Sincerely,
Jonas Feld
Quality Manager, ClearLabel Packaging

questions.question: What caused the labeling problem, according to the letter?

options.text: A shortage of Apex bottle caps
A printer calibration error on Line B
Incorrect shipping addresses on PO-7731
Damage during overnight freight

questions.correctAnswer: A printer calibration error on Line B
questions.explanation: Feld writes that inspection confirmed a printer calibration error on Line B caused the defect.
questions.commonMistake: Blaming overnight freight, which is how the replacement will ship, not the cause.

questions.question: What must Ms. Okonkwo do if she wants a partial restock instead of a full replacement?

options.text: Pay the $180 return-shipping credit first
Notify Jonas Feld by Tuesday at noon
Recalibrate Line B herself
Cancel PO-7731 permanently

questions.correctAnswer: Notify Jonas Feld by Tuesday at noon
questions.explanation: The letter offers a partial restock if she notifies Feld by Tuesday at noon; otherwise the full 2,400-unit replacement proceeds.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking she must cancel the purchase order to change the restock size.

questions.question: In the letter, the word “credit” most nearly means

options.text: a loan application
an amount returned to a customer’s account
a job recommendation
a packaging design award

questions.correctAnswer: an amount returned to a customer’s account
questions.explanation: “Credit your account $180” means ClearLabel will put $180 back on Ms. Okonkwo’s account for return shipping.
questions.commonMistake: Reading “credit” as praise or a loan rather than an account adjustment.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this letter?

options.text: To deny responsibility for the labeling defect
To explain the cause of a defect and offer replacements and a credit
To request a larger future order of Apex bottles
To announce the permanent shutdown of Line B

questions.correctAnswer: To explain the cause of a defect and offer replacements and a credit
questions.explanation: Feld confirms the cause, describes corrective steps, promises free overnight replacement, and offers a $180 credit plus an optional partial restock.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing only on the apology tone and missing the concrete remedies.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: BrightPath Consulting — Tuition Assistance Request Form
passages.body:
Employee name: Lena Park
Department: Client Analytics
Course title: Advanced SQL for Business Reporting
Provider: Metro Tech Institute
Course dates: Oct 6 – Dec 12 (Tuesday evenings)
Tuition: $1,280
Employee contribution (per policy): 25% = $320
Amount requested from BrightPath: $960

Eligibility checklist (all required boxes must be checked):
☑ Full-time employee for at least 12 months
☑ Course related to current role or approved career path
☑ Manager approval attached
☐ Prior tuition assistance repaid if employee left within 12 months of reimbursement (marked N/A — first request)

Instructions: Submit this form and the course syllabus to hr-learning@brightpath.example at least 15 business days before the course start date. Reimbursement is paid after a grade of B or higher (or Pass) is documented. Maximum annual assistance: $2,000 per employee.

Manager signature: R. Soto · Date: Sep 2

questions.question: How much tuition assistance is Lena Park requesting from BrightPath?
questions.explanation: The form lists amount requested from BrightPath as $960. $320 is the employee’s 25% share; $1,280 is full tuition; $2,000 is the annual maximum.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting full tuition or the annual cap instead of the requested company share.

questions.question: According to the form instructions, which of the following is NOT required before reimbursement is paid?

options.text: Submitting the form and syllabus at least 15 business days before the course starts
Documenting a grade of B or higher (or Pass)
Manager approval attached
Completing the course on weekday mornings only

questions.correctAnswer: Completing the course on weekday mornings only
questions.explanation: A–C appear in the eligibility checklist or instructions. The course is listed as Tuesday evenings; nothing requires morning-only attendance.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming evening courses are ineligible because many workplaces favor daytime training.

questions.question: What can be inferred about Lena Park’s tuition-assistance history at BrightPath?

options.text: She has already used the full $2,000 annual maximum
This appears to be her first tuition-assistance request
She left the company within the past 12 months
She failed to get manager approval

questions.correctAnswer: This appears to be her first tuition-assistance request
questions.explanation: The repayment checkbox is marked N/A with the note “first request,” and manager approval is checked — so this is her first assistance request.
questions.commonMistake: Misreading the N/A repayment line as evidence she left the company.

questions.question: In the form, the word “reimbursement” most nearly means

options.text: a warning before dismissal
payment that covers an approved expense after it is incurred
a schedule of evening classes
a temporary employee badge

questions.correctAnswer: payment that covers an approved expense after it is incurred
questions.explanation: Reimbursement is paid after a qualifying grade is documented — money returned/paid for the approved course cost.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing reimbursement with advance payment before the course begins.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Email — Thursday setup checklist
passages.body:
From: Dana Ruiz
To: Booth crew — GreenLeaf Expo
Subject: Thursday setup checklist

Team — Reminder that our booth (Hall C, Booth 214) must be ready by 8:00 a.m. Thursday for the buyer walkthrough. Please arrive by 6:30 a.m. with badges. Marcus is bringing the demo tablets; Priya has the printed catalogs.

I requested two extra power strips from Facilities — confirmation #EX-902. If they are not at the booth by 7:00 a.m., call the service desk at extension 4400.

passages.label: B
passages.heading: GREENLEAF EXPO — Exhibitor logistics notice
passages.body:
Week of October 20

Parking:
• Lot A (main entrance): Exhibitor unloading Wednesday 4:00–10:00 p.m. only. Vehicles must exit Lot A by 10:00 p.m. Overnight parking is not allowed in Lot A.

questions.question: According to Dana’s email, where is the company’s booth located?

options.text: Hall B lobby
Hall C, Booth 214
Lot D, space 4400
Exhibitor Services desk

questions.correctAnswer: Hall C, Booth 214
questions.explanation: Dana reminds the crew that the booth is Hall C, Booth 214. Hall B is where permits are picked up.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the Exhibitor Services location (Hall B) with the booth location.

questions.question: According to the venue notice, when do exhibitor hall doors open on Thursday?
questions.explanation: The notice states doors open for exhibitors at 6:00 a.m. Dana asks the crew to arrive by 6:30; the walkthrough is at 8:00; public opening is 9:30.
questions.commonMistake: Using Dana’s arrival time (6:30) instead of the official door-open time.

questions.question: Why does Dana tell the crew not to leave the van in Lot A after 10:00 p.m. Wednesday?

options.text: Lot A closes permanently after the expo
Overnight parking in Lot A is not allowed
Lot A is reserved only for buyer walkthrough guests
Power strips can only be delivered to Lot D

questions.correctAnswer: Overnight parking in Lot A is not allowed
questions.explanation: Dana points to the venue notice: Lot A is for Wednesday unloading until 10:00 p.m., and overnight parking there is forbidden; overnight parking is Lot D with a permit.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming Lot A is only for buyers rather than reading the overnight restriction.

questions.question: Based on the email and the notice, what should the crew do to park the van overnight before Thursday’s setup?

options.text: Leave it in Lot A after unloading because the booth booking is confirmed
Move it to Lot D and obtain a dashboard permit from Exhibitor Services by 9:00 p.m. Wednesday
Park in Hall C next to Booth 214 overnight
Keep the van in Lot A and file a power request at extension 4400

questions.correctAnswer: Move it to Lot D and obtain a dashboard permit from Exhibitor Services by 9:00 p.m. Wednesday
questions.explanation: Dana says overnight parking is Lot D only; the notice requires a dashboard permit from Exhibitor Services (Hall B lobby) until 9:00 p.m. Wednesday. Lot A overnight is banned.
questions.commonMistake: Relying only on Dana’s Lot D mention and missing the permit deadline in the notice.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT stated in either passage?

options.text: The buyer walkthrough begins at 8:00 a.m. Thursday
Marcus is bringing the demo tablets
Public show floor opens at 9:30 a.m.
Priya will pick up the Lot D parking permit

questions.correctAnswer: Priya will pick up the Lot D parking permit
questions.explanation: A–C appear in the email or notice. Priya has printed catalogs; neither text assigns her to pick up the parking permit.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming Priya handles all logistics because she has the catalogs.

sets.title: Hot-desking pilot results at Northvale Labs

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Northvale Labs News — Desk-booking pilot wraps up
passages.body:
Northvale Labs has completed a three-month pilot of a desk-booking system on floors 4 and 5. Under the program, employees reserve a workstation through the DeskFlex app by 5:00 p.m. the day before. Unclaimed desks are released at 9:30 a.m. for same-day booking.

Facilities manager Carla Nguyen reported that average desk occupancy rose from 61 percent to 78 percent, and the company reclaimed twelve unused private offices for collaboration rooms. Survey responses were mostly positive, though night-shift lab technicians said the 5:00 p.m. cutoff left them with fewer morning options.

Leadership will expand DeskFlex to floor 3 in January but will keep dedicated desks for the night-shift team. Training sessions for new users will be held during the first week of December.

questions.question: According to the article, by what time must employees reserve a desk for the following day?

options.text: Noon
The first week of December

questions.explanation: Employees reserve through DeskFlex by 5:00 p.m. the day before. 9:30 a.m. is when unclaimed desks are released.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the reservation deadline with the 9:30 a.m. release time for unclaimed desks.

questions.question: What can be inferred about night-shift lab technicians?

options.text: They will lose all assigned desks when DeskFlex expands to floor 3.
They preferred the pilot more than any other group surveyed.
Their work schedule made the advance booking deadline inconvenient.
They already use DeskFlex successfully on floor 3.

questions.correctAnswer: Their work schedule made the advance booking deadline inconvenient.
questions.explanation: They said the 5:00 p.m. cutoff left fewer morning options, and leadership will keep dedicated desks for them—implying the booking window conflicted with night-shift hours.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming they will lose desks, when the article says dedicated desks will be kept for them.

questions.question: In the article, the word “reclaimed” is closest in meaning to

options.text: purchased for the first time
recovered for a new use
permanently closed to staff
rented to another company

questions.correctAnswer: recovered for a new use
questions.explanation: Twelve unused private offices were recovered and turned into collaboration rooms—taken back for a different purpose.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing “permanently closed,” which contradicts converting them into collaboration rooms.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the article?

options.text: Northvale Labs is ending remote work and requiring daily attendance.
A desk-booking pilot improved occupancy and will expand with some adjustments.
Floor 3 will replace DeskFlex with assigned seating next month.
Carla Nguyen is leaving her role after the pilot ends.

questions.correctAnswer: A desk-booking pilot improved occupancy and will expand with some adjustments.
questions.explanation: The article reports higher occupancy, space recovered for collaboration rooms, expansion to floor 3, and dedicated desks kept for night-shift staff.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing only on the night-shift exception and missing the overall positive pilot outcome.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: FleetCare Pro — Keep your company vehicles on the road
passages.body:
Tired of last-minute repair surprises? FleetCare Pro offers scheduled maintenance for corporate fleets of 5–200 vehicles.

Autumn Business Package (valid Sept 1 – Nov 30):
• Oil change, tire rotation, and multi-point inspection — $89 per vehicle
• Free loaner car for repairs lasting more than four hours
• Priority booking window: weekdays 7:00 a.m. – 9:00 a.m.
• 10% discount on brake service when you enroll three or more vehicles

Mobile vans available within 25 miles of our Riverside depot. Evening appointments after 6:00 p.m. are offered only for fleets of 20+ vehicles.

Call 555-0148 or visit fleetcarepro.com/business. New accounts receive a complimentary cabin air filter on the first visit.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this advertisement?

options.text: To sell new company cars at the Riverside depot
To promote a seasonal corporate fleet maintenance package
To announce that FleetCare Pro is closing evening service
To recruit mechanics for mobile repair vans

questions.correctAnswer: To promote a seasonal corporate fleet maintenance package
questions.explanation: The ad markets the Autumn Business Package for corporate fleets with pricing, perks, and enrollment details.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking it sells vehicles rather than maintenance services.

questions.question: How much does the autumn package cost per vehicle?

options.text: 10% of brake service
It is free for new accounts

questions.explanation: The package (oil change, tire rotation, multi-point inspection) is listed at $89 per vehicle. New accounts get a free cabin air filter, not a free package.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming the complimentary air filter means the whole package is free.

questions.question: In the advertisement, the word “complimentary” is closest in meaning to

options.text: required
expensive
provided at no charge
available only online

questions.correctAnswer: provided at no charge
questions.explanation: New accounts receive a complimentary cabin air filter—meaning it is given free on the first visit.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing “complimentary” with “complementary” (something that goes well with something else).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT offered under the Autumn Business Package?

options.text: A free loaner car when repairs take more than four hours
Priority booking on weekday mornings
A 10% brake-service discount when enrolling three or more vehicles
Evening appointments after 6:00 p.m. for every fleet size

questions.correctAnswer: Evening appointments after 6:00 p.m. for every fleet size
questions.explanation: Evening appointments after 6:00 p.m. are only for fleets of 20+ vehicles, not every fleet. A–C are explicitly included.

sets.title: Bike-to-work stipend chat and parking notice

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Team chat — Commute benefits
passages.body:
Maya Chen (HR): Reminder — Bike-to-Work stipend applications close Friday at noon. Upload a photo of your bike lock receipt in the portal under “Active Commute.”
Omar Siddiq: Does the $150 cover a new helmet too, or only locks?
Maya Chen: Helmets, lights, and locks all count. Instant commute cards do NOT.
Priya Nair: I already got approved last month. Can I apply again this quarter?
Maya Chen: One stipend per employee per calendar year. Priya, you’re set until January.
Omar Siddiq: Also — is Covered Bike Rack B still closed?
Maya Chen: Check the facilities notice. Rack A is fine; I think B has a schedule change this week.

passages.heading: Facilities Notice — Covered bicycle parking
passages.body:
Effective Monday–Wednesday this week, Covered Bike Rack B (east entrance) will be offline while the canopy roof is resealed. Please use Covered Bike Rack A (west entrance) or the open racks by Lot C.

Rack A capacity: 40 bikes. Arrive before 8:15 a.m. for the best chance of a spot; overflow bikes may be tagged and moved to Lot C open racks after 9:00 a.m.

Helmets and small gear may be stored in the new lockers beside Rack A (badge access, first-come). Do not chain bikes to handrails or the loading dock.

questions.question: According to the chat, when do Bike-to-Work stipend applications close?

options.text: Monday at 8:15 a.m.
Friday at noon
After 9:00 a.m. Wednesday
In January only

questions.correctAnswer: Friday at noon
questions.explanation: Maya states applications close Friday at noon. January refers to when Priya can apply again.
questions.commonMistake: Mixing the stipend deadline with bike-rack timing from the notice.

questions.question: According to the notice, how many bikes can Covered Bike Rack A hold?
questions.explanation: The notice states Rack A capacity is 40 bikes.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing capacity with the $150 stipend amount from the chat.

questions.question: What is suggested about Priya Nair?

options.text: She can submit a second stipend application this week.
She has already used her stipend for this calendar year.
She works only at the east entrance near Rack B.
She needs to upload a lock receipt by Friday noon.

questions.correctAnswer: She has already used her stipend for this calendar year.
questions.explanation: Priya was approved last month; Maya says one stipend per employee per year and that Priya is set until January.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking she must still apply by Friday because Maya’s reminder was sent to the whole chat.

questions.question: Based on the chat and the notice, what should Omar do if he bikes to work on Tuesday?

options.text: Use Covered Bike Rack B at the east entrance as usual
Chain his bike to the loading-dock handrail until Rack B reopens
Use Covered Bike Rack A or the open racks by Lot C because Rack B is offline
Skip applying for the stipend until Rack B’s canopy is resealed

questions.correctAnswer: Use Covered Bike Rack A or the open racks by Lot C because Rack B is offline
questions.explanation: Omar asks if Rack B is still closed; Maya points him to the notice. The notice confirms Rack B is offline Monday–Wednesday and directs riders to Rack A or Lot C open racks.
questions.commonMistake: Answering from the chat alone without checking the notice’s Rack B closure dates.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT covered by the Bike-to-Work stipend, according to the chat?

options.text: Helmets
Lights
Locks
Instant commute cards

questions.correctAnswer: Instant commute cards
questions.explanation: Maya says helmets, lights, and locks all count, but instant commute cards do NOT.
questions.commonMistake: Missing Maya’s explicit exclusion of instant commute cards.

sets.title: Mandatory MFA enrollment for remote staff

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Subject: Action required — enroll in MFA by September 30
passages.body:
From: Keiko Tanaka, IT Security
To: All remote and hybrid staff

Dear colleagues,

Starting October 1, all staff who access company systems from outside the office must use multi-factor authentication (MFA). Enrollment is now open in the Security Portal.

Please complete enrollment by September 30. After that date, remote logins without MFA will be blocked. On-site desktop users are exempt until January, when MFA will extend to all accounts.

If you lose your phone or cannot enroll, contact the IT Help Desk at extension 2200 before September 28 so we can issue a hardware token. Walk-in token pickup is available in Building A, Room 112, weekdays 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m.

A 12-minute tutorial video is posted on the intranet under Security > MFA Guide.

Thank you for helping protect client data.

Keiko Tanaka
IT Security Manager

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this email?

options.text: To announce that the Security Portal will close in January
To require remote and hybrid staff to enroll in MFA by a deadline
To replace all employee phones with hardware tokens
To cancel on-site desktop access until October 1

questions.correctAnswer: To require remote and hybrid staff to enroll in MFA by a deadline
questions.explanation: The email announces that remote/hybrid staff must enroll in MFA by September 30 before remote logins without MFA are blocked on October 1.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing on the January extension for on-site users and missing the primary MFA enrollment requirement.

questions.question: By when must staff complete MFA enrollment?

options.text: September 28
September 30
October 1
January 1

questions.correctAnswer: September 30
questions.explanation: Enrollment must be completed by September 30. September 28 is the help-desk contact deadline for tokens; October 1 is when remote logins without MFA are blocked.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the enrollment deadline with the October 1 blocking date or the September 28 token request cutoff.

questions.question: In the email, the word “exempt” is closest in meaning to

options.text: required to finish early
not subject to the rule for now
unable to use the intranet
responsible for training others

questions.correctAnswer: not subject to the rule for now
questions.explanation: On-site desktop users are exempt until January, meaning they do not have to follow the MFA rule yet.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing a meaning related to training or deadlines instead of temporary exclusion from the rule.

questions.question: What can be inferred about employees who work only at on-site desktops?

options.text: They must enroll in MFA before September 30
They will lose intranet access on October 1
They are not required to use MFA until January
They must pick up a hardware token in Room 112

questions.correctAnswer: They are not required to use MFA until January
questions.explanation: The email states on-site desktop users are exempt until January, when MFA extends to all accounts.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming the September 30 deadline applies to every employee, including on-site-only staff.

passages.heading: MEMORANDUM — Q3 expense report cutoff
passages.body:
To: All department managers
From: Luis Ortega, Finance
Date: September 12, 2026
Subject: Q3 expense report cutoff — revised

Please remind your teams that Q3 expense reports must be submitted in the ExpenseHub portal by Friday, September 25, at 5:00 p.m. Reports filed after that time will post to Q4 and may delay reimbursements until late October.

Paper receipts are no longer accepted for meals under $25; upload a digital photo instead. Travel expenses over $500 still require a pre-approval code (TRAV-Q3) before submission.

Managers should approve pending reports by Monday, September 28, so Payroll can process reimbursements on October 3.

Questions: finance@northbridge.example

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this memo?

options.text: To announce that ExpenseHub will shut down in October
To update managers on the Q3 expense deadline and related rules
To cancel all travel over $500 for the rest of the year
To hire additional staff for the Payroll department

questions.correctAnswer: To update managers on the Q3 expense deadline and related rules
questions.explanation: The memo revises the Q3 submission cutoff, clarifies receipt rules, and sets a manager approval date so reimbursements can be processed.
questions.commonMistake: Treating the travel pre-approval detail as the memo’s overall purpose.

questions.question: When must Q3 expense reports be submitted?

options.text: September 12 at noon
September 25 at 5:00 p.m.
September 28 at 5:00 p.m.
October 3 at 5:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswer: September 25 at 5:00 p.m.
questions.explanation: Reports must be submitted by Friday, September 25, at 5:00 p.m. September 28 is the manager approval deadline; October 3 is the reimbursement processing date.
questions.commonMistake: Mixing up the employee submission deadline with the manager approval date.

questions.question: What will most likely happen if an employee submits a Q3 report on September 26?

options.text: It will be paid on October 3 with other Q3 reports
It will be rejected and must be mailed as a paper form
It will post to Q4 and reimbursement may be delayed until late October
It will require a TRAV-Q3 code even for meals under $25

questions.correctAnswer: It will post to Q4 and reimbursement may be delayed until late October
questions.explanation: The memo states reports filed after September 25 will post to Q4 and may delay reimbursements until late October.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming late reports are still processed with the October 3 Q3 reimbursement run.

questions.question: According to the memo, which of the following is NOT stated?

options.text: Meals under $25 need a digital photo instead of a paper receipt
Travel over $500 still needs a TRAV-Q3 pre-approval code
Managers should approve pending reports by September 28
Employees may submit Q3 reports by email if ExpenseHub is busy

questions.correctAnswer: Employees may submit Q3 reports by email if ExpenseHub is busy
questions.explanation: The memo requires submission in ExpenseHub and never offers email as an alternative. The other options are explicitly stated.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a true detail (such as the photo-receipt rule) instead of the option that is not mentioned.

passages.label: A
passages.heading: Letter — Coral Analytics to Meridian Retail Group
passages.body:
September 8, 2026

Ms. Hannah Cho
Operations Director
Meridian Retail Group

Dear Ms. Cho,

Thank you for selecting Coral Analytics for your warehouse inventory audit. We confirm that fieldwork will begin Monday, September 21, at your Springfield distribution center.

Our lead auditor, Rajiv Mehta, will arrive at 8:00 a.m. with two associates. Please arrange badge access and a secure workstation near the receiving dock. The on-site phase is expected to last four business days; a draft findings report will follow within ten business days after fieldwork ends.

As agreed, the fixed fee is $14,800, with 40% due upon kickoff and the balance upon delivery of the final report. Kindly return the signed Statement of Work by September 15 so we can reserve the audit team.

We look forward to a productive engagement.

Sincerely,
Elena Vargas
Client Partner, Coral Analytics

questions.question: What is the main purpose of this letter?

options.text: To request a discount on Meridian’s warehouse lease
To confirm audit start details and request a signed Statement of Work
To announce that Coral Analytics is hiring new auditors
To cancel the Springfield distribution center visit

questions.correctAnswer: To confirm audit start details and request a signed Statement of Work
questions.explanation: Elena confirms the September 21 fieldwork start, logistics, fee schedule, and asks for the signed Statement of Work by September 15.
questions.commonMistake: Focusing only on the fee amount and missing the confirmation-and-SOW purpose.

questions.question: When will fieldwork at the Springfield distribution center begin?

options.text: September 8
September 15
September 21
Ten business days after kickoff

questions.correctAnswer: September 21
questions.explanation: The letter confirms fieldwork begins Monday, September 21. September 15 is the SOW return deadline; the draft report follows within ten business days after fieldwork ends.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing the Statement of Work deadline with the fieldwork start date.

questions.question: In the letter, the word “fieldwork” most nearly means

options.text: on-site audit work at the client location
online training for new warehouse staff
marketing research about retail competitors
construction work near the receiving dock

questions.correctAnswer: on-site audit work at the client location
questions.explanation: Fieldwork refers to the auditors’ on-site phase at the Springfield distribution center lasting four business days.
questions.commonMistake: Reading “field” literally as construction or outdoor physical labor.

questions.question: What will most likely happen if Meridian does not return the signed Statement of Work by September 15?

options.text: The audit fee will automatically drop below $14,800
Coral may be unable to reserve the audit team as planned
Rajiv Mehta will start fieldwork one day early
Badge access will be arranged by Coral Analytics

questions.correctAnswer: Coral may be unable to reserve the audit team as planned
questions.explanation: Elena asks for the signed SOW by September 15 specifically so Coral can reserve the audit team.
questions.commonMistake: Inferring a fee change or schedule change that the letter never suggests.
